atomic_claims.text: Under the frozen nonempty-shore semantics, K1 meets average degree <d and girth >=g for all d>0 and g>=3 but has no matching cut.
Every disconnected finite simple graph of order at least two has an empty matching cut.
In a connected graph, singleton-edge cuts are exactly bridges and are matching cuts.
A nonempty forest has a matching cut exactly when its order is at least two; with c components its average degree is 2-2c/n.
On the explicitly restricted domain n>=2, average degree <2 guarantees a singleton-shore matching cut, so g=3 works for 0<d<=2. The unrestricted root retains K1.
Among nonempty finite simple graphs of average degree at most two, the only graphs without matching cuts are K1 and C3.
A nontrivial qualifying graph without a matching cut must be connected, bridgeless and have minimum degree at least two; this does not remove K1 from the literal contract.
